# artifactkeeper_repository_allowlist (Resource)

The package allowlist of a virtual conda channel (Artifact Keeper 1.11.0): while enabled, a package from a Remote member is served only if an entry admits it; hosted members are not filtered. A singleton keyed by repository key; destroy removes the list.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Serve only vetted packages from conda-forge through the virtual channel.
resource "artifactkeeper_repository_allowlist" "conda" {
  repository_key = "conda-virtual"
  enabled        = true
  entries = [
    { name = "numpy", version = ">=1.26,<3" },
    { name = "pandas" },
    { name = "pytorch", subdirs = ["linux-64"] },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the list is enforced. An enabled empty list admits nothing from Remote members.
- `repository_key` (String) Key of the virtual conda repository. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `entries` (Attributes List) Admitted packages. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--entries))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Equal to `repository_key`.

<a id="nestedatt--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `entries`

Required:

- `name` (String) Exact conda package name or a glob (`*`, `?`), case-insensitive.

Optional:

- `subdirs` (List of String) Subdirs the entry applies to (`noarch`, `linux-64`, ...). Omit for every subdir.
- `version` (String) Conda version spec (`2.2.3`, `2.2.*`, `>=2,<3`). Omit for every version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import artifactkeeper_repository_allowlist.conda conda-virtual
```
